title: Time
description: Hours worked, each tied to the work it was for, and invoices made from them. A client company says who bills it, its rate, terms and whether HST is charged.

types.title: Time entry
types.description: Time spent on one piece of work on one day, as hours or as a block from a start to an end. A planned block is time set aside, not yet worked: it counts toward nothing and is never invoiced until the owner confirms it (logged). The title says what was done in a few words; the note says more. Make it part of the work it was for (a project or task); the client is the company that work involves.

date.description: The day the work was done.

hours.description: Hours spent, e.g. 1.5. When start and end are both given, the hours are the time between them.

start.description: When the block of work began, for an entry drawn on the calendar.

end.description: When the block of work ended.

billable.description: Whether it goes on an invoice.

rate.description: An hourly rate for this entry only, when it is not the client's.

types.title: Routine
types.description: A block that repeats: the same hours on the same days of the week, like dinner from 17:00 to 19:00 every day. Nothing is stored for a day: the calendar draws it where it falls. Made part of a piece of work, each day it falls on is planned time for that work, which the owner confirms as it happened; one that is part of nothing only holds the time.

from_time.description: When it begins each day, as 17:00, in Toronto.

to_time.description: When it ends each day, as 19:00.

days.description: The days of the week it falls on, 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday. Every day when left out.

starts.description: The first day it falls on. From when it was made when left out.

until.description: The last day it falls on, when it ends.

skip.description: Days it does not fall on after all, as 2026-10-15.

moved.description: Days it falls at other hours: each day with its from and to, as {"2026-10-15": ["18:00", "20:00"]}.

done.description: Days of work the owner has confirmed: each made a time entry, and is no longer drawn from the routine.

types.title: Invoice
types.description: A bill to a client for time entries, kept as a document: its note is the invoice as sent, fixed when made. Read, print or share it as any document.

billed_by.description: The company or person the invoice is from.

period_from.description: The first day of the work billed.

period_to.description: The last day of the work billed.

paid.description: What has been paid so far.

paid_on.description: The day of the last payment.

payments.description: Each payment received: date, amount and method (e-Transfer, EFT, cheque, card).

rate.description: Hourly rate billed to this client.

terms_days.description: Days until an invoice is due.

hst.description: Whether 13% HST is charged to this client.

billed_by.description: Id of the company or person who bills this client, e.g. your own company.

hst_number.description: Its own HST number, when it bills.

payment.description: How to pay, as it goes on invoices: one way per line, e.g. "Interac e-Transfer to pay@example.com (autodeposit)" and "EFT: institution 004, transit 12345, account 1234567".

hst_number.description: HST number, when they bill as a sole proprietor.

payment.description: How to pay, as it goes on invoices: one way per line, e.g. "Interac e-Transfer to pay@example.com (autodeposit)" and "EFT: institution 004, transit 12345, account 1234567".

links.title: bills
links.description: The invoice bills this time entry.

rules.say: "{title}" is a routine: only a person confirms a day of it, on the Time screen. Its days wait there under To confirm.
"{title}" is planned time: only a person confirms that it happened, on the Time screen. It waits there under To confirm.
"{title}" already has that number from the same biller: invoice numbers are not reused.

views.description: Today for Home: the owner's blocks today (time entries and the days routines fall on), in the order they fall, each with its hours and the work it is for, then how many planned blocks wait to be confirmed on the Time screen.

Time logged over a span of days, by day and by client; what is logged but not yet invoiced, by client; and invoices not yet paid (invoices: outstanding, overdue with how many days, drafts, owed_total). This week (Monday to Sunday) unless from and to are given.

A week as a calendar, Monday to Sunday (this week unless from is given): for each day, the owner's blocks (owner: time entries, with start and end where they were logged as blocks, else hours alone, and the days routines fall on) and the agents' lanes (agents: one list per agent at work at once, each block a stretch of a session, with the work it was on). Every block has from_hour and to_hour (hours since that day's midnight in the workspace's time zone), hours, the work and the project it counts toward; projects lists them in the order the page colours them. An owner block with status planned is time set aside: a day's hours leave it out and planned counts it. to_confirm lists planned time whose end has passed, in any week, for the owner to confirm (status logged), as planned or as it happened, or drop. Only a person can confirm it: an agent that tries is refused.

from.description: Any day in the week, or its Monday, as 2026-10-12.

actions.title: Log time
actions.description: Record time spent on a piece of work: how many hours, on which day (today unless given, in the workspace's time zone), what was done in a few words, and a note if there is more to say. Or a block, with start and end in place of hours: the hours are the time between, and the day is the day it began. planned: true sets the time aside without saying it was worked: it counts toward nothing and is not invoiced until the owner confirms it. work is the id of the project, task or client it was for; the client billed is the company that work, or what it sits in, involves. Search for the work first. Say what you logged back to the person, with the client (answer.client).

work.description: Id of the project, task or client company the time was for.

hours.description: Hours spent, e.g. 1.5. Needed unless start and end are given.

start.description: When the block began, as a date-time with its offset, e.g. 2026-10-15T09:30:00-04:00.

what.description: What was done, in a few words: the entry's title.

note.description: More about the work, if there is more to say.

date.description: The day, as 2026-10-15. Today when left out.

billable.description: false for time that is not to be invoiced.

rate.description: An hourly rate for this entry only, when it is not the client's.

planned.description: true for time set aside ahead, not yet worked.

actions.title: Draft an invoice
actions.description: Draft an invoice to a client company for its billable time not yet invoiced, up to a day (today unless given). The client says who bills it (billed_by), its rate, terms_days, currency and whether HST is charged (hst). The invoice is a document, part of the client, numbered INV-<year>-<n> for its biller; its entries are marked invoiced. It stays a draft until the owner sends it; time_invoice_void undoes it.

from.description: Only time from this day, as 2026-10-01.

to.description: Only time up to this day. Today when left out.

actions.title: Record a payment
actions.description: Record a payment received on an invoice: the day (today unless given), the amount (all that is still owed unless given) and how it came (e-Transfer, EFT, cheque, card). Paid in full, the invoice closes as paid; a part-payment leaves it open with what is still owed. Record what the owner says came in.

amount.description: What was received. All that is still owed when left out.

date.description: The day it was received, as 2026-10-15. Today when left out.

method.description: How it came, e.g. e-Transfer, EFT, cheque.

actions.title: Void an invoice
actions.description: Void an invoice: it is kept, marked void, and its time entries go back to being logged, to be invoiced again.
